Subject: Geo readiness: Chicago + Frankfurt + Hong Kong pilot SKU ask (Vizenta)

Team —

Vizenta is ready to move forward with a three-region pilot and they want estimated committed SKU sizing + an operational handoff plan. Key asks pulled from their requirements spreadsheet (attached): sustained 24/7 throughput for 20k monthly active inference sessions, an expected peak of ~120 QPS across regions, and a strict PII isolation requirement for EU traffic.

High level we need:
- a recommended committed pool (US/EU/APAC) with burst lanes and canary cadence
- lead times for capacity allocation (how many weeks before we can guarantee sustained nodes)
- fallback plan (hosted variants) and SLA impact for tri-region routing

Please reply with concrete numbers and risks. I want a draft SOW + internal ops checklist by EOD Friday so we can include with the commercial proposal. Attachment: vizenta_requirements.xlsx (from customer).

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Geo readiness: Chicago + Frankfurt + Hong Kong pilot SKU ask (Vizenta)

Laura / team —

Quick sizing proposal based on the spreadsheet:
- US (Chicago) committed pool: 8 sustained A100-equivalent GPUs + 4 burst lanes for weekends/launch spikes
  - Target SLO: 95th pctk latency < 320ms for conversational workloads
- EU (Frankfurt) committed pool: 4 sustained GPUs + 2 burst lanes (data residency requirement needs Frankfurt pinned)
- APAC (Hong Kong microregion): 2 sustained GPUs, no committed burst lanes initially — recommend requesting a 6-week pilot with ability to convert to burst reserve if usage justifies

Notes / risks:
- Lead time: procurement and capacity assignment for committed pools is ~4–6 weeks from signature for those exact SKU guarantees; burst lanes can be enabled in 7–10 days but are subject to global utilization at the time of enablement.
- Cost math: rough blended committed monthly run-rate across the three regions will be ~ $85k–$110k depending on negotiated committed discounts and quantization profiles. I can model per-token deltas if we need.
- Fallback: If we can’t meet committed SKUs in APAC at go-live, recommend routing APAC traffic to hosted Hong Kong-compatible variant with explicit regional header + reduced latency SLA (we must disclose to customer).

I’ll draft an ops checklist (capacity tickets, canary schedule, traffic gating) and share.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Capacity Strategist, Redwood Inference

Hi Laura / Ben —

Thanks for the quick reply. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 120 QPS peak is global; we expect an even split US 50%, EU 30%, APAC 20% during pilot traffic patterns.
- EU data must remain in Frankfurt for that 30% slice — SOC2 and infosec sign-off hinge on this.
- Hong Kong microregion needs to be <120ms median for our latency-sensitive routing (we will accept slightly higher P95).

Procurement note: our finance team needs a clear committed SKU line item and a 60-day trial-with-right-to-terminate clause spelled out. We have a DocuSign SOW template but can accept Redwood's SOW if the commitment and exit terms are clean.

I've attached our annotated requirements spreadsheet used earlier (vizenta_requirements.xlsx). We'll review any SOW you send and loop Kevin from engineering for technical validation.

-Emma

Emma — thanks for the clarifications. Quick operational play: 

1) Canary & gating plan (week-level timeline):
   - Week 0 (post-sign): provision Frankfurt + Chicago committed nodes in parallel; assign APAC warm standby (2 GPUs) in Hong Kong.
   - Week 1–2: internal canary (10% traffic) routing to tri-region; smoke tests for KV cache warmup and prefix caching.
   - Week 3–4: escalate to 50% traffic with on-call runbook active; collect latency / token-cost deltas.
   - Week 5–8: full pilot (100%) with weekly retros and SLA health checks; option to convert Hong Kong warm standby to committed if median latency target not met.

2) Fallback & transparency: if capacity constraints force routing to hosted Hong Kong-compatible variants, we will require a short-term SLA amendment and customer acknowledgement — we can include a clause in the SOW that defines the fallback window and remediation path.

3) Action items for Redwood ops (owners):
   - Ben: finalize exact SKU models and buffer sizing (this email).
   - Priyom: prep canary runbook and traffic-split config, include KV-cache priming steps.
   - Marissa/Commercial: draft SOW with 60-day trial language + committed pricing bands; include DocuSign link for signature.

I will coordinate a technical readiness call with Kevin next week (30–45m).

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Infrastructure Planning, Redwood Inference
